tips.title: Tips for a good photo
tips.body: Photograph one leaf, fill the frame, use natural light, and place it on a plain background.
leafcheck.title: This doesn't look like a leaf
leafcheck.body: LeafCare AI only recognises leaves of 14 crops, so other photos give meaningless results. Please use a close-up of a single leaf. If this is a leaf, you can still run the diagnosis.
uncertain.title: We're not sure about this one
uncertain.body: The model is only {confidence} confident, so treat this result as a guess. Please try a clearer, closer photo of a single leaf on a plain background, in good light.
home.gradcam_caption: Red and yellow areas influenced the prediction most; blue areas mattered least. If the hot spots sit on the background rather than the leaf, try a new photo.
advice.healthy_symptoms: No disease symptoms detected. Healthy leaves are evenly coloured, without spots, mould, holes or curling.
advice.healthy_treatment: No treatment needed. Keep monitoring the plant regularly.
advice.disclaimer: Informational only — consult a local agricultural officer before applying any chemicals.
advice.translated: This advice was machine-translated from English. Check with a local expert, or switch to English, before acting on it.
history.title: Scan history

history.empty_body: Open Diagnose in the menu at the top, analyse a leaf, and it will appear here.
about.title: About the model
about.subtitle: LeafCare AI uses transfer learning: a network pre-trained on millions of everyday photos is fine-tuned to recognise 38 leaf conditions across 14 crops.
about.results: Results on the held-out test set
about.no_metrics_body: Train the model with notebooks/train_model.ipynb in Google Colab, then copy models/metrics.json and reports/figures/ into this project to see the results here.
about.confusion_caption: Each row is the true class; a bright diagonal means most images are classified correctly.
about.dataset_body:
- **PlantVillage**: about 54,000 labelled leaf images, 38 classes across 14 crops, including a *healthy* class for 12 of the crops.
- Split **80 / 10 / 10** into train / validation / test sets, stratified by class so every class is represented in the same proportion (random seed 42).
- Images are resized to 224 × 224 pixels, using the same function in training and in this app.
about.architecture_body: EfficientNetB0 is a compact convolutional network (about 4 million parameters) that is fast enough for a web app. Its final convolutional layer, `top_conv`, is also what Grad-CAM uses to draw the heatmap on the Diagnose page.
about.training_body:
1. **Data augmentation** (random flips, rotation, zoom, brightness, contrast and slight cropping) so the model copes better with real-world photos.
2. **Phase 1, feature extraction:** the pre-trained backbone is frozen and only the new classification head is trained (about 5 epochs, Adam, learning rate 1e-3).
3. **Phase 2, fine-tuning:** the top ~30% of the backbone is unfrozen (BatchNorm layers stay frozen) and trained with a much smaller learning rate (1e-5, about 10 epochs).
4. **Early stopping** (patience 3) keeps the weights from the best validation epoch.
about.limit_lab_body: PlantVillage leaves were photographed one at a time on plain backgrounds. Accuracy on real field photos (cluttered backgrounds, several leaves, shadows, blur) is noticeably lower than the test score above.
about.limit_classes_body: The model can only recognise the 14 crops and 38 conditions it was trained on. A leaf from any other plant or disease will still be forced into one of them, which is why low-confidence results show a warning.
about.limit_expert_title: Not a substitute for an expert.
about.limit_expert_body: Advice is general and informational. Always confirm with an agronomist or local agricultural officer before applying treatments.
sdg.title: Fighting hunger, one leaf at a time
sdg.subtitle: Early, accurate disease detection helps farmers save more of what they grow and use fewer chemicals doing it.
sdg.sdg2_p1: Target 2.4 asks for farming practices that raise productivity while protecting ecosystems. Plant diseases work against both: a blight noticed a week too late can wipe out a field, and the usual response, spraying everything, harms soil and water.
sdg.sdg2_p2: LeafCare AI gives a first opinion in seconds from an ordinary phone photo, so problems are noticed earlier, when they are cheaper and easier to control, and a crop's yield is protected.
sdg.sdg12_p1: When farmers can't tell diseases apart, they often use the wrong product or too much of it, just in case. Knowing which disease is present means treating only what is needed, starting with cultural and organic measures.
sdg.sdg12_p2: That supports responsible chemical management and reduces food lost before harvest, both central aims of SDG 12.
sdg.detect_body: Spot disease from a photo before it spreads across the field.
sdg.understand_body: See the crop, the likely disease, and a heatmap showing why.
sdg.act_body: Get prevention-first advice and a reminder to consult local experts.
sdg.who_body:
- **Smallholder farmers**, who produce a large share of the world's food but often have limited access to plant-health experts.
- **Extension workers**, as a quick triage tool to prioritise field visits.
- **Students and home gardeners** learning to recognise common crop diseases.
sdg.responsible_title: A first opinion, not a final diagnosis
sdg.responsible_body: The model was trained on lab-style photos and only knows 38 conditions. It flags uncertain results, explains where it looked, and always recommends confirming with a local agricultural officer before applying chemicals.
